prompt:
Use case: ui-mockup
Asset type: high-fidelity desktop landscape product design comp for a native macOS development environment
Primary request: Design one polished Operate-mode workspace for an AI-native iOS development environment. The visual concept is a blueprint-layer workbench: the interface should feel like precise engineering layers laid over a restrained native macOS tool, not a generic SaaS dashboard.
Scene/backdrop: A single edge-to-edge native macOS application window, straight-on orthographic view, no desktop environment around it.
Style/medium: High-fidelity realistic UI design comp, native macOS visual language, crisp product screenshot quality.
Composition/framing: 16:10 desktop landscape. Code-led tri-pane composition. At the far left, a compact vertical mode rail with four icon-plus-label destinations using the exact labels “Code”, “Agent”, “App”, “Verify”; Code is selected. Beside it, a narrow file outline showing a small iOS project tree with ProfileView.swift selected. The dominant center pane is a source editor titled “ProfileView.swift”, with line numbers and credible, legible SwiftUI code for a profile screen. A narrow right pane is the live App/evidence inspector: show a small iPhone simulator preview of a Profile screen, a semantic hierarchy/evidence section beneath it, and one clear verified state. Across the top, use a native compact toolbar with repository and scheme context and exact actions “Build”, “Run”, “Stop”. The lower edge may include a very compact task/build status strip, but must not become a fourth pane.
Color palette: Restrained graphite and charcoal surfaces, blueprint blue for active structure and selection, verified green only for successful evidence, subtle warm-neutral text. Avoid cyan overload.
Visual system: Fine one-pixel dividers, square-to-small-radius native controls, exact alignment, high information density, strong editor hierarchy, subtle blueprint-grid or drafting registration details only in the App/evidence inspector background. No gradients. No glassmorphism. No floating cards. No card grid.
Typography: Native macOS sans-serif UI typography plus monospace editor typography. All requested labels must be spelled exactly and be clearly readable.
Text (verbatim): “Code”, “Agent”, “App”, “Verify”, “Build”, “Run”, “Stop”, “ProfileView.swift”, “Verified”
Constraints: The result must look implementable as a native SwiftUI/AppKit macOS app. Keep the editor visually dominant. Use a single coherent workbench shell. Show a believable source tree, credible Swift code, a Profile app preview, semantic UI evidence, and a visible verified green status. No fake company names, no commercial claims, no metrics, no pricing, no marketing slogan.
Avoid: generic web dashboard styling, excessive rounded rectangles, gradients, translucency, frosted glass, floating modular cards, card grids, neon, pure black, huge headings, browser chrome, fake logos, testimonial language, unreadably tiny text, duplicated panes, shipping/distribution UI, TestFlight, real-device controls.
